focus_areas.area: DNS enumeration (Route53 public zones, wildcard records, A/CNAME exposure)
API Gateway stages (authentication posture, logging, WAF)
Internet-facing Load Balancers (WAF, TLS, non-standard ports)
Elastic IPs and NAT Gateway public IP inventory
Attack surface score and overall external exposure rating

rule.title: Unauthenticated API Endpoints
rule.description: API Gateway stages or routes with AuthorizationType=NONE are Critical if they serve sensitive data or trigger side effects
rule.action: Flag each unauthenticated stage. Check if stage name contains "prod", "production", or has no environment qualifier (assume prod).

rule.title: Public Lambda Function URLs
rule.description: AuthType=NONE on Lambda Function URLs is Critical — anyone on the internet can invoke the function
rule.action: Flag each public Lambda URL. Cross-reference with vulns evidence (lambda-environment-variables.json) if available to check for secret exposure.

rule.title: DNS Wildcards
rule.description: Wildcard records (*.) expose the full internal service naming scheme to attackers
rule.action: Flag all wildcard A/CNAME records. Assess what services they might expose based on target names.

rule.title: Public Load Balancers Without WAF
rule.description: Internet-facing ALBs without WAF are vulnerable to OWASP attacks. High risk.
rule.action: Flag each internet-facing LB where WafWebAclArn is null or empty.

rule.title: Attack Surface Score
rule.action: Generate a finding for RECON-015 if score ≥5.0. Use the score and rating from attack-surface-score.json.

evidence_focus.note:
Output must be written in English.
This skill produces external attack surface intelligence, NOT internal configuration findings. Think like an external attacker with no credentials: - What can they see and invoke from the internet? - Which entry points have no authentication? - Which DNS records reveal architecture?
Gating rules for this skill: - If route53-zones.json has no public zones, SKIP RECON-001, RECON-004, RECON-013. - If api-gateway-stages.json has total_apis=0, SKIP RECON-002, RECON-009, RECON-014. - If lambda-urls.json has total_function_urls=0, SKIP RECON-005, RECON-018. - If load-balancer-dns.json has total_load_balancers=0, SKIP RECON-007, RECON-011, RECON-017. - If public-endpoints.json has elastic_ip_count=0, SKIP RECON-003, RECON-016. - If cloudfront-origins.json has total_distributions=0, SKIP RECON-006, RECON-012, RECON-019. - If attack-surface-score.json has score < 3.0, generate RECON-020 (minimal attack surface) instead.
DO NOT generate findings based on absence of evidence. Only report what is confirmed present.

focus.check: Records exposing internal naming (dev, staging, internal, admin, bastion in Name)
Count of public zones vs. private zones
Entries where IsPublic=true and WafWebAclArn is null
HTTP listeners (Protocol=HTTP, Port=80) on internet-facing LBs
Distributions where WebAclId is null or empty
Origins pointing to S3 buckets (may indicate direct S3 access)

irrefutable_evidence_guide.requirement: Every RECON finding MUST include in evidence_snippet the exact attack surface metadata:

for_dns_zones.field: IsPrivate flag (true/false) — MUST be false for public exposure findings
Exact record Name and Type (A, CNAME, MX, etc.) if exposed
If zone exposes architecture: list sensitive keywords found (pci, admin, internal, db, staging, prod, vpc)

for_eip.field: Associated SecurityGroupIds and permissive Ingress rules (0.0.0.0/0, exact ports)
InstanceName + port mapping to show complete attack chain

steps.step: 1. Go to API Gateway > [API Name] > Routes/Methods
3. Choose: Cognito User Pool, IAM, or Lambda Authorizer
4. For REST APIs: Create Usage Plan + API Key for rate limiting
5. Test authentication with curl: expect 401 Unauthorized without credentials
1. Go to Lambda > [Function] > Configuration > Function URL
2. Change Auth type from NONE to AWS_IAM
3. Update callers to sign requests with SigV4
4. If public access is needed, implement auth within the function handler
5. Restrict CORS: set AllowOrigins to specific trusted domains
1. Go to WAF & Shield > Web ACLs > Create Web ACL
3. Add managed rule groups: AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet, AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet
4. Add rate-limiting rule (e.g. 2000 req/5min per IP)
